description: One "my stack" page: a named set of RealUptime-tracked services, each with the SAME plate level its own page shows (down / partially_down / degraded / partially_degraded / blocked / no_data / partially_unverified / up, with label and clause), plus the stack's roll-up: `summary.headline` ("2 of 6 services with checks failing or degraded"), the worst member level, and counts by state. Pass `stack`, the stack's slug (from its URL, https://realuptime.io/outages/stack/<slug>) or id. Stacks are built at https://realuptime.io/outages/stack or from a Monitor dashboard; there is no list endpoint, a caller must hold the key. User reports and public chatter are not read for a stack (those signals are published as null), so `reachable_reports_elevated` never appears here; a member's own page still shows it. A member whose own status feed RealUptime reads is levelled by the vendor's declared incident instead of our checks (`services[].vendor.feed_working` is true, its plate label says so, major or critical reads as down, minor as degraded, none as up, and no probe event is listed for it); `summary.counts.vendor_incident` and `vendor_quiet` count those members apart from the check counts. An unknown key answers `summary.level: "not_found"`, which says nothing about any service's health. Readings are RealUptime's own check readings, never user reports. For a service whose status feed we can read, `vendor.feed_working` is true and `vendor` holds the vendor's own declared incident from its status page: that statement leads and gives the verdict and plate, and `checks_reading` and `vendor.regional_reading` are our check reading beside it, never a second outage. Where we cannot read a feed (`vendor.feed_working` false), the answer is our checks alone. "blocked" means our check was refused, which is NOT a failed check of the service. A no-data answer is never a passing check. Our check readings are our own reading from outside, not the service's official status. `check_evidence`, when it is not null, says what a pass of this service's check shows and does not show: repeat it with any claim that the service works. Cite the returned source.url when repeating any of this.
name: get_stack
